Meta Introduces Subscription Tiers to Limit and Charge for Hyperlinks on Facebook Pages

28 Oct 2026, 08:27 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Business Desk · Source: www.npr.org

Image: www.npr.org — Creative Commons

Share this article
WhatsAppFacebookTelegram
Key takeawaysSocial media platforms have historically prioritized keeping users within their own ecosystems, and recent platform updates reflect new monetization strategies regarding outbound traffic. Meta has rolled out a system limiting how many hyperlinks Facebook Pages can post

Social media platforms have historically prioritized keeping users within their own ecosystems, and recent platform updates reflect new monetization strategies regarding outbound traffic. Meta has rolled out a system limiting how many hyperlinks Facebook Pages can post for free, introducing paid tiers for publishers and businesses wanting to share more external links.

Facebook Page Link Limits and Pricing

Under the updated rules, Facebook Page operators are restricted to two free hyperlinks per month. To post more frequently, Meta now offers tiered subscription plans:

  • Meta One Advanced Plan: Costing $49.99 per month, this tier allows users to include up to eight hyperlinks in posts or reels.
  • Max Plan: Costing $499 per month, this option permits an unlimited amount of hyperlinks.

Industry observers note that this move aligns with broader social media industry trends. For example, studies by organizations like Nieman Lab have previously highlighted how platform algorithms can deprioritize or penalize posts containing outbound links, such as those used by news publishers on platforms like X.

Platform Incentives and User Impact

According to David Evans, managing director at the consulting firm BRG, attention is the primary economic driver for social media platforms. Platforms rely on content to attract consumer attention and subsequently sell targeted advertising access to marketers. Because external links divert users away from the site or app, platforms have commercial incentives to discourage or monetize outbound traffic.

The policy change has drawn criticism from digital creators and business owners. Ashley Gullen, who runs a game design company, publicly criticized the shift on the decentralized platform Mastodon, describing the monetization of basic page functions as an unwelcome platform development.

Practical Implications and Verification

For businesses, community groups, and publishers relying on Facebook Pages to drive traffic, these new limits necessitate a reevaluation of organic social media strategies. Organizations must now decide whether the cost of a Meta subscription tier is justified by the referral traffic generated.

Readers seeking to verify these changes can review platform announcements directly through official channels or read the original reporting provided by public media outlets. The original reporting and broader business context were detailed in a publication by NPR available at [NPR's Planet Money](https://www.npr.org/sections/planet-money/2026/10/23/nx-s1-6012726/why-meta-is-charging-to-post-more-hyperlinks).

What Is Confirmed vs. Unknown

  • Confirmed: Facebook Pages are limited to two free hyperlinks per month under the current structure, with paid tiers priced at $49.99 and $499 per month providing higher allowances.
  • Unknown: The long-term adoption rates of these subscription tiers among small businesses and major publishers remain to be seen, as do potential future adjustments to platform pricing or feature limits.
